summary.headline: UTI AMC Q2 FY27 standalone core PAT rose 31% YoY to Rs 136 crore, while reported PAT fell 14% YoY to Rs 143 crore.
summary.overview: UTI AMC reported Q2 FY27 standalone core income of Rs 324 crore (+2% YoY, +5% QoQ) and core PAT of Rs 136 crore (+31% YoY). Consolidated core income was Rs 398 crore and consolidated core PAT Rs 131 crore. Average mutual fund AUM rose to Rs 4.02 lakh crore from Rs 3.93 lakh crore in Q1, with net sales of about Rs 5,720 crore, but equity and hybrid outflows increased, with Flexi-Cap a key drag. Management said several funds were improving on performance, and that SIP AUM was flat QoQ at Rs 45,572 crore. The CEO did not attend the call due to a family emergency.

segments.name: Mutual fund (domestic)
segments.commentary: Average MF AUM Rs 4.02 lakh crore; equity-oriented (active plus passive) 72% of AUM vs about 70% in Q1. Group AUM Rs 16.28 lakh crore at 30 Sept 2026.

segments.name: UTI Pension Fund (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM about Rs 4.32 lakh crore at 30 Sept 2026, up about 10.97% YoY from Rs 3.89 lakh crore; 24.01% share of NPS industry AUM. 169 new corporates onboarded Apr-Oct 2026.

segments.name: UTI International
segments.commentary: AUM US$1.67 billion (about Rs 16,063 crore) at 30 Sept 2026; clients in more than 30 countries. Revenue flat QoQ; two new fund launches planned by end Q3 or Q4 FY27.

segments.name: UTI Alternatives
segments.commentary: AUM about Rs 4,045 crore, up 52% from Rs 2,669 crore a year earlier. SDOF IV crossed Rs 1,000 crore (Rs 1,131 crore) against a Rs 1,500 crore target plus Rs 500 crore greenshoe.

guidance_outlook: Standalone employee cost guided at about Rs 95 crore per quarter and consolidated at about Rs 130 crore per quarter, maintained for full FY27.
Hybrid Long-Short SIF fund to launch in Q3 FY27; further SIF product decisions over next one to two years depending on demand.
Two UTI International fund launches expected by end Q3 or Q4 FY27.
Board policy to distribute about 90-95% of profit as dividend; no plans for special dividend or deployment of surplus cash.
Passive growth expected to dilute revenue yield marginally but support PAT margin, as there is no incremental cost.
capex_capacity: Standalone employee cost guided at about Rs 95 crore per quarter; consolidated about Rs 130 crore per quarter.
Research coverage expanded to 480 companies in H1 FY27; 36 IPOs evaluated and six participated.
255 branches across the country, staffed for sales and distributor engagement.
Process optimisation generated about Rs 4.22 crore in savings; 10,690 sales-team training hours delivered up to Sept 2026.
demand_pricing: Industry equity inflows Rs 92,333 crore in Q2 FY27 (H1 Rs 1.83 lakh crore); September equity inflows Rs 38,307 crore; SIP contribution a record Rs 32,490 crore in September.
UTI gross SIP inflows Rs 2,583 crore in Q2 (H1 Rs 5,085 crore); SIP AUM Rs 45,572 crore, flat vs Rs 45,595 crore in June 2026.
UTI share of industry new SIP registrations by volume 4.08% in Q2; 5.96 lakh new SIPs, 87% sourced digitally; average SIP ticket about Rs 3,100.
Revenue yields: equity and hybrid about 73-74 bps; ETF and index about 8 bps; cash and arbitrage about 11 bps; fixed income about 20-21 bps; weighted average about 31 bps, flat QoQ per management.
Flexi-Cap accounts for about 20.3% of SIP inflows (19.3% last year); sectoral and thematic 16%, mid-cap 15%, large and mid-cap 12.7%. Small-cap took 10.4% of pure equity inflows in the quarter.
Equity redemptions came mainly from banks and national distributors; some from MFDs and direct channel. SIP closure rate about 70% vs industry about 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net outflows rise to about Rs 800 crore in equity and Rs 300 crore in hybrid, and will employee numbers keep falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Flexi-Cap saw large outflows despite some inflows; the fund is now in the first quartile on three-month performance. Two blend-strategy funds are in the top two quartiles. Management guided standalone employee cost at about Rs 95 crore and consolidated at about Rs 130 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is UTI gaining share in new SIP registrations, and how are ticket sizes trending?
qa_highlights.answer: New SIP registration share is close to 4%, with many SIPs staying. Average ticket size is about Rs 3,100, up over time.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 AUM growth came from net inflows versus market appreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Average AUM rose by about Rs 10,000 crore, of which about Rs 5,720 crore came from net sales.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise yields and reasons for the sequential yield movement?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity and hybrid about 73-74 bps, ETF/index about 8 bps, cash/arbitrage 11 bps, fixed income 20-21 bps. Weighted average flat at about 31 bps; marginal change from repricing commissions after the SEBI TER-to-BER change, passed on to intermediaries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for UTI International and the SIF strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Two new UTI International fund launches planned by end Q3 or Q4. First SIF launch is the Hybrid Long-Short fund in Q3; product choices will follow demand over one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cash around 45-50% of market cap, and should it be returned to shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no plans for special dividend or distributing surplus cash; it will continue paying about 90-95% of profit as dividend, citing the need for standalone capital for growth.

risks_watch: Flexi-Cap and blend-strategy fund performance must stabilise before inflows recover; equity outflows elevated in Q2.
Redemptions from banks and national distributors; direct channel stickiness weaker per analyst question.
Passive mix growth dilutes revenue yield (about 31 bps weighted average); PAT margin is expected to offset.
Industry small-cap and mid-cap flows moderating; October trends not yet available.
Large cash balance (analyst-cited at 45-50% of market cap) with no capital deployment plan announced.
summary.management_tone: Confident on structural industry growth and SIP and new-investor metrics, but cautious and somewhat evasive on equity outflows, October trends and small-cap flow data. Management offered offline follow-up on figures it did not have on hand.
key_quotes: Even though short -term volatility is an inherent part of equity investing, the structural drivers of the mutual fund industry, including the economic growth, rising income, broader investor participation, and financialisation of household savings, remain intact.

So, there might be a marginal dilution as far as the revenue yields are concerned, but the PAT margin numbers should keep on improving it because there's no additional incremental cost to run these passive strategies.
SIP is a slow-gain process. In a month, even if we double our SIP number, it will not add very high numbers.
